children: Biocon Ltd. on Friday, September 25, said its Malaysia arm received approval from the UK drug regulator for its new drug product fill finish unit for Semglee (insulin glargine) at its insulin manufacturing facility in Malaysia.
The company said the Medicines and Healthcare Products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) in UK gave its nod for the same.
Earlier this month, Biocon MD and CEO Shreehas P Tambe told
that the company's insulin business can reach the $1 billion revenue mark soon. It i seeing strong demand for insulin and traction for newer products such as aflibercept supporting growth.
Beyond insulin, the company has a portfolio of over 30 biosimilars, including newer products like Aflibercept and established ones such as trastuzumab and pegfilgrastim.

The company is also expecting double-digit revenue growth in biosimilars, while it targets margins in the mid-20% range. It has recently combined its biologics and generics businesses and is working to improve the profitability of the generics segment that had earlier operated at low-teen margins. Tambe told CNBC-TV18 that getting the combined business to the mid-20s will represent a substantial improvement.
Biocon reported its first quarter earnings last month.
Its net profit surged to ₹141 crore from ₹31.4 crore last year. Its revenue increased 16% to ₹4,336 crore from ₹3,942 crore in the first quarter last year.

The company's earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA) increased 10.6% to ₹847.2 crore from ₹766.1 crore and its margin expanded to 19.54% from 19.43% in the year-ago period.
Shares of Biocon are trading 0.6% lower on Friday at ₹384.55. The stock is flat for the year so far, down only 0.8%.

title: Biocon Malaysia arm gets UK regulator approval for Semglee fill finish unit
